== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' lived at Irvine, Ayrshire, where the parish register names him as the father of three children baptised between 1741 and 1747. Their mother was [[Nasmith-38|Helen Nasmith]], named in the same entries:

* [[Glasgow-4116|John Glasgow]], baptised 6 August 1741
* [[Glasgow-4110|Allan Glasgow]], baptised 22 May 1743
* [[Glasgow-4128|Susanna Glasgow]], baptised 29 March 1747

No birth or baptism record for James himself has been found, so his birth is placed before 1722, the year by which he must have been born to father John in 1741. Irvine is inferred from his children's baptisms and is not independently recorded.<ref name="IrvineOPR">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Irvine, Ayrshire, Old Parish Register OPR 595/1; the individual baptism entries are cited on each child's profile, for example [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575071&tab=this John Glasgow, 1741].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Possible Irvine birth family ===

Select John [[Glasgow-2475]] of the Irvine Isabell Kyle/Kelle household as the possible working father of James [[Glasgow-4157]], Helen Nasmith’s partner, at 58% subjective confidence. The leading explanation identifies the later James with John and Isabell’s James, baptised at Irvine on 19 August 1711 ([[Glasgow-4100]]). This joins a specific recorded birth family to a specific later household in the same parish. Assuming infant baptism, that James would be about thirty when John was born in August 1741 and about thirty-five at Susanna’s 1747 birth. The later household’s first known son is John, agreeing with the proposed paternal grandfather. Same-parish continuity, a comfortable adult chronology and this modest naming clue together favour this family over the younger 1721 comparison. None independently proves the identification.

The 58% assesses the complete father proposition, including the uncertain baptism-to-adult identity. No source names the 1741–1747 father’s own parents, and no residence, trade or witness links the households. Baptism is not necessarily near birth, John is a common forename, and the first known child is not necessarily the eldest child. The 1711 and 1721 ages are illustrative infant-baptism assumptions, not recorded ages. James [[Glasgow-4157]]’s before-1722 birth is an inherited adult-age estimate, not a 1722 birth or a hard biological boundary. Do not use that estimate to prefer or exclude a candidate. All dates and identities remain unchanged. The original registers are uninspected; maintained Findmypast transcripts are being reassessed, not newly discovered.

Retain James [[Glasgow-4158]] as an unselected alternative father at 26%, through possible identification of Helen Nasmith’s partner with his son James [[Glasgow-4129]], baptised at Irvine on 11 April 1721 to James and Margaret Rae. If baptised as an infant, he would be about twenty at the 1741 child’s birth: young but fully possible, not excluded. The Rae household and its Margaret/Marion distinction remain as previously assessed. James [[Glasgow-1932]], baptised at Kilwinning in 1707 to John Glasgow and Mary Gemill, and James [[Glasgow-1131]], indexed at Kilbirnie in 1718 to John Glasgow and Agnes Ferguson, remain broader compatible comparisons; their father’s name could also explain a John child, so naming is not unique. An unrepresented family is also possible. No new individual percentages are assigned to these unselected broader identity comparisons. Another compatible model identifies Helen Nasmith’s partner with the older Rae-household James [[Glasgow-4158]] himself, after a different partnership. His inherited age estimate would make him at least about thirty-nine in 1741, which does not exclude this model. No spouse death or remarriage is established. This is distinct from the 26% model making the later man a son of James [[Glasgow-4158]]; neither identity is merged. Hugh [[Glasgow-3109]]’s existing uncertain attachment belongs to the elder account and is not transferred to James [[Glasgow-4157]].

This is one newly selected possible father, not a confident relationship or a source discovery. The Irvine James, John, Allan and Susanna household provisionally joins the larger working component; supported and confident connectivity do not gain this 58% edge. James’s documented fatherhood of the three children remains separately 98%. His identification with the Prosperity shipmaster in 1740 remains unresolved and supplies no family bridge. John [[Glasgow-2475]]’s own uncertain upstream pedigree is not strengthened. Isabell Kyle is not selected as James [[Glasgow-4157]]’s mother. [[Glasgow-4100]] and [[Glasgow-4157]] may be two accounts of one person: no merge is performed and the working profile count is not a count of distinct proved people or two independently established James brothers. Resolve the possible duplicate before any live attachment or merger.

Compare the original Irvine 1711 and 1721 baptism entries with the 1741, 1743 and 1747 entries for occupations, addresses and witnesses; seek a James–Helen marriage or earlier child. Those details could distinguish the birth identities without relying on naming. Reassess the 58% and 26% together when a discriminating record appears.<ref name="IrvineUpstream2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3572963&tab=this Findmypast, Irvine OPR595/1 p.16, James Glasgow baptism, 19 August 1711; parents John Glasgow and Isabell Kelle; SCOT/OPR/BAP/3572963, maintained transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573667&tab=this Findmypast, Irvine OPR595/1 p.29, James Glasgow baptism, 11 April 1721; parents James Glasgow and Margt Rae; SCOT/OPR/BAP/3573667, maintained transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575071&tab=this Findmypast, Irvine OPR595/1, John Glasgow baptism, 1741; maintained 3 September 2026 transcript, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3575071]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575202&tab=this Findmypast, Irvine OPR595/1, Allan Glasgow baptism, 1743; maintained 3 September 2026 transcript, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3575202]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575478&tab=this Findmypast, Irvine OPR595/1, Susanna Glasgow baptism, 1747; maintained 3 September 2026 transcript, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3575478].</ref>


=== Irvine baptism household ===

James [[Glasgow-4157]] is the documented father of Allan [[Glasgow-4110]] at 98% subjective confidence. Allan’s maintained Findmypast baptism transcript explicitly names James Glasgow and Helen Nasmith at Irvine on 22 May 1743, with birth on 15 May. James-4157 is the existing adult account defined by this same three-child household, not a name-only match to a separately known shipmaster. John’s 1741 baptism names James Glasgow and Helen Nasmith, and Susanna’s 1747 entry names Jas Glasgow and Helen Macsmith. The shared parish, father, maternal forename and compatible sequence support one household, with Macsmith retained as the indexed maternal variant. Allan’s own entry supplies the father directly; the siblings independently support the identification.

The 98% applies to the father of these record-defined children, allowing for derivative transcription and an uninspected original. The saved Findmypast transcripts were captured on 3 September 2026 and are reused here; no original or new source is claimed inspected today. This neither identifies James with the Prosperity shipmaster in 1740 nor gives him a named father. Other Irvine James profiles remain compatible comparisons for those distinct identity questions. No birth, death, occupation, marriage, mother or upstream parent is inferred from this decision.

Inspect the original Irvine OPR595/1 entries for the maternal Macsmith/Nasmith reading and any residence, occupation or witnesses that distinguish James’s birth family. His before-1722 birth remains an adult-age estimate. The 1711 Irvine James, son of John Glasgow and Isabell Kelle, and the 1721 James, son of James and Margaret Rae, are compatible later-identity comparisons; neither is selected solely from name, age or parish.<ref name="IrvineHousehold2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575071&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Irvine OPR595/1, John Glasgow, 6 August 1741, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3575071; maintained 3 September 2026 transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575202&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Irvine OPR595/1, Allan Glasgow, 22 May 1743, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3575202; maintained 3 September 2026 transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575478&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Irvine OPR595/1, Susanna Glasgow, 29 March 1747, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3575478; maintained 3 September 2026 transcript].</ref>


James and Helen are linked only by the recurring father and mother names in the Irvine register. No record of James's own parents, birth or death has been found.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow, master of the Prosperity of Irvine. James Glasgow is named in the Greenock arrival list headed “Greenock, August 12”: “The Prosperity of Irvine, James Glasgow, from Northcopen.” The item was published in The Caledonian Mercury on 18 August 1740, page 3.<ref>The Caledonian Mercury, 18 August 1740, page 3, Greenock shipping list; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394559372/ record].</ref> The ship–homeport–master–origin format supports reading James as the shipmaster. No age, relatives or personal residence are stated. Irvine is the ship’s homeport and Greenock the reporting locality; neither proves James’s birthplace. Northcopen is retained without an unverified modern-place identification. The identification remains uncertain.
